summary.headline: GHCL Textiles Q1 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to Rs.410 crores, with EBITDA of Rs.70 crores (~17% margin) helped by cotton inventory gains.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs.410 crores (up 52% YoY), EBITDA Rs.70 crores and PAT Rs.39 crores. Management said the spread widened to about Rs.155/kg (with packing) from Rs.138/kg in Q4 FY26, helped by cotton bought earlier at lower prices. Fabric reached 16% of sales (vs 9% a year ago) as the first 15 of 40 planned knitting machines ran. Management guided a normalised EBITDA margin of 14-15% for FY27 and 16-18% once ready-to-cut fabric capacity is in place, and set a target of Rs.2,000 crores revenue by FY29.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA margin ~17% (vs ~12% last year, per management)

financial_highlights.value: ~10-12% of sales price increase attributed to inventory gain (sales prices up ~20-24%)

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: 89% of yarn production sold as yarn; 11% converted to fabric. Spinning utilisation ~99% per management, and 98%+ per the CEO's answer on volume. No new yarn capacity planned beyond knitting.

segments.name: Fabric (woven and knitted)
segments.commentary: Fabric is ~16% of sales, split roughly 50:50 woven and knitted. The 15 knitting machines run at 80-85% utilisation, with Q1 the first full quarter. Greige fabric contributed about Rs.65 crores this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin of 14-15% for FY27; Q1's inventory gain will not recur. Q2 spread expected slightly below Q1 but similar to the current level.
Ready-to-cut fabric integration expected to lift normalised EBITDA margin to 16-18%.
Revenue target of Rs.2,000 crores by FY29, from about Rs.1,350 crores in FY26 (14% growth); management expects FY27 at about Rs.1,500 crores.
FY27 capex of about Rs.100-120 crores including modernisation; about Rs.350-400 crores earmarked for ready-to-cut fabric facilities, subject to shareholder approval.
Remaining 25 knitting machines to be received in Q2 and Q3 FY27, bringing the total to 40 by Q3-end.
11 MW ground solar commissioning now expected December 2026 (~Rs.6 crores/year savings, full benefit next year); 3 MW rooftop solar live since January (~Rs.2 crores/year).
capex_capacity: Total installed renewable capacity ~65 MW, with an additional 11 MW ground solar in progress (commissioning slipped to December 2026 due to MNRE/ALMM list changes).
First 50 knitting machines installed and commercial production stabilised; 15 knitting machines received so far and 25 more to follow in phases through Q3 FY27.

PM MITRA Park (Tamil Nadu): land allotted in Q4 FY26; park completion targeted December 2027; GHCL must complete within three years of allotment. Fabric/processing plant planned for CY28, with part work possibly earlier.
In-house knitting capacity expected to be about 12-15% of total yarn production once all 40 machines are running.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices (domestic): Rs.62,000/candy in April, Rs.67,000 in May, Rs.64,000 in June, and back to about Rs.68,000-70,000 by the call. NY futures reached 80 cents/lb at end-June.

Order book healthy with 1.5-2 months of forward booking maintained. Exports to Europe (Germany, Italy and others) were strong in Q1; GHCL has no direct US/UK exposure and sells through process houses and garmenters.
Chinese yarn demand from India has risen since December 2025 (partly on lower Chinese cotton output); GHCL itself exports little to China. Q1 saw some slowdown in that demand.
Management says domestic textile demand is growing 6-8% YoY. Cotton is now at parity with imported cotton, supporting export competitiveness.
Cotton stock is held till November-December; further inventory plans depend on the monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cotton inventory position and the current spread?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is covered until the new season (Nov-Dec). Current spread is ~Rs.160/kg before packing (~Rs.155 after), up from ~Rs.138/kg in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin sustainable, and what does fabric contribution look like over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads should stay better than last year and similar in Q2, then depend on the market. Fabric to reach 30-40% of revenue after about three years as a ready-to-cut supplier, up from 15-16% now.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 EBITDA came from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales prices rose ~20-24%, but inventory gain accounted for only ~10-12%. The rest came from better pricing, customer mix and strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the Q1 spread given rising cotton prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread can be held at current cotton levels of Rs.68,000-69,000/candy, but may compress if yarn prices lag. Q2 expected slightly below Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any capacity expansion on the yarn side besides knitting?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Only knitting machines are in the pipeline, plus about Rs.350 crores of capex for ready-to-cut fabric.

qa_highlights.question: How is the order book for H2 FY27, and are there US/UK/EU orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book healthy at 1.5-2 months forward. Strong European demand in Q1; no direct US/UK orders since GHCL supplies yarn and greige fabric as a tier-two vendor.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected once ready-to-cut is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Normalised margin 14-15% for FY27; 16-18% after vertical integration (ready-to-cut fabric).

qa_highlights.question: What incentives come with the PM MITRA Park project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited capital subsidy of about Rs.100-125 crores on a ~Rs.1,000 crore total investment under TN incentive schemes. The first inspection is done and the file is moving. The CEO said debt concessions were not a main factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the roadmap to double revenue to Rs.2,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue grows about 14% a year from ~Rs.1,350 crores in FY26 to reach Rs.2,000 crores by FY29. Growth comes from greige fabric and ready-to-cut fabric (Rs.350-400 crores of turnover at 1:1 or 1:0.8 asset turnover).

risks_watch: Cotton price path: domestic cotton rose to about Rs.68,000-70,000/candy; management expects spreads to compress from Q2 as low-cost inventory is consumed and yarn prices may lag cotton.
Q1 EBITDA includes an inventory gain (~10-12% of the 20-24% sales price rise); management says this will not recur and normalised FY27 margin is 14-15%.
Spread guidance: Q2 expected slightly below Q1 but similar to current levels; full-year spread guided above last year but no firm number given.
Execution of 40 knitting machines (15 received, 25 more in Q2-Q3 FY27) and 80-85% utilisation of the first 15 machines.
11 MW ground solar commissioning slipped to December 2026 due to MNRE/ALMM list changes.

PM MITRA Park: park completion targeted December 2027, company must commission within three years of allotment; fabric plant planned for CY28; Rs.350-400 crore ready-to-cut capex subject to shareholder approval.
Incentive clarity: capital subsidy of about Rs.100-125 crore cited by management, but a CFO-level answer on concessional debt was not given; management said it would revert on this.
Tariff and FTA details (US 10% reset, possible zero duty for 20%+ US cotton use, EU FTA timing) still not fully clear per management.
key_quotes: So, currently, our spreads are about Rs. 160 per kilo without the packing cost.
So, definitely, we have come from 12% which was there last year to about 17% this quarter. We think the normalized margin for this year will be about 14%-15%, right?
But even with 40 knitting machines, our total in-house knitting capacity would be only about 12-15% of our overall yarn production.
Fabric will become a significant part of our overall top line, probably in the region of about 30% -40%, which is right now at 15% -16%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FY26-27 outlook, with specific numbers on spreads, capex and the Rs.2,000 crore FY29 revenue goal. Cautious on the sustainability of Q1 margins: management repeatedly flagged that the inventory gain will not recur and that spreads may compress as cotton costs rise, and it deferred on several specifics (PM MITRA incentives, US tariff details, the full-year spread level).

adds.what: 15 more knitting machines (of 40 total) to be received in Q2-Q3 FY27; first 15 already running
11 MW ground solar (renewable, not production capacity)
PM MITRA Park Tamil Nadu fabric/processing plant (ready-to-cut), planned CY28

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to about Rs.1,500 crores (~11% over FY26 Rs.1,350 crores) and Rs.2,000 crores by FY29, backed by 25 remaining knitting machines due Q2-Q3 FY27 and ~Rs.350 crores ready-to-cut capex, but the ready-to-cut plant is only planned for CY28 and the margin guidance points to normalising Q1's inventory gain, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Normalised margin 14-15% in FY27 rising to 16-18% only once ready-to-cut fabric is integrated (planned CY28), so expansion depends on that plant and on spreads holding above last year's level.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2-Q3 FY27 for knitting machines; CY28 for ready-to-cut fabr
rows.why: Spinning utilisation at 98%+ with no new yarn capacity planned; 25 of 40 knitting machines still to arrive in Q2-Q3 FY27 and ~Rs.350 crores ready-to-cut capex planned for CY28 under PM MITRA Park, though the plant is only planned, not firmly dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to ~Rs.1,500 crores (~11% over Rs.1,350 crores in FY26) and Rs.2,000 crores by FY29, backed by 25 knitting machines still to arrive and 98%+ spinning utilisation capping yarn volumes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 98%+ and ~Rs.350-400 crores ready-to-cut capex earmarked, subject to shareholder approval; a formal capex approval is the next step.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management's FY27 revenue guide of ~Rs.1,500 crores (~11% growth) and 14-15% normalised margin are conservative only in form; the call flagged spread compression as cotton rises to Rs.68,000-70,000/candy.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management already guided Q2 spread slightly below Q1 (Q1 ~Rs.155/kg), and normalised FY27 EBITDA margin of 14-15% sits well below Q1's ~17% as the ~10-12% sales-price inventory gain does not recur.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Knitting machines are scaling from 15 to 40 with 80-85% utilisation on the first 15, so knitted fabric is a new product line ramping; ready-to-cut fabric is planned for CY28.

rows.label: Order book 1.5-2 months forward; strong European demand in Q1
rows.why: Order book is healthy at 1.5-2 months of forward booking and European demand (Germany, Italy) was strong in Q1, though GHCL has no direct US/UK exposure.

rows.label: 11 MW ground solar commissioning slipped to December 2026
rows.why: Expected savings of ~Rs.6 crores/year from the 11 MW ground solar plus ~Rs.2 crores/year from the 3 MW rooftop already live since January, but the commissioning slipped on MNRE/ALMM changes.

rows.label: PM MITRA Park capital subsidy of Rs.100-125 crores
rows.why: Management cited a capital subsidy of about Rs.100-125 crores on ~Rs.1,000 crores total investment; the first inspection is done and the file is moving, but concessional debt terms were not confirmed.
